Extract selected records from a FASTQ file

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
extract_fastq_records.Rd

Extracts FASTQ records corresponding to selected indices and writes them to an output file. The input is processed in chunks to limit memory usage, allowing large FASTQ files to be sampled or subsetted without loading the entire file into memory.

Usage

extract_fastq_records(fastq, outfile, keep_lookup, chunk_records = 25000)

Arguments

fastq

Character string giving the path to the input FASTQ file. Files ending in .gz are treated as gzip-compressed.

outfile

Character string giving the path to the output FASTQ file. A filename ending in .gz produces gzip-compressed output.

keep_lookup

Logical vector indicating which FASTQ records should be retained. The i-th element corresponds to the i-th record in the input FASTQ file.

chunk_records

Integer specifying the maximum number of FASTQ records to process in each chunk. Since each FASTQ record contains four lines, chunk_records determines the number of lines read at each iteration. Defaults to 2.5e4.

Value

Invisibly returns the total number of FASTQ records processed.

Details

Both compressed (.gz) and uncompressed FASTQ files are supported through open_any.

FASTQ records are assumed to consist of exactly four lines. The input file is read in chunks of chunk_records records, and only records corresponding to TRUE values in keep_lookup are written to the output file.

The function preserves the order of records from the input file. Selected records are written in their original order, regardless of how the selected indices were generated.

A file is considered gzip-compressed when its filename ends in .gz. The output is written using the same connection mechanism as the input, allowing compressed output without requiring the entire file to be held in memory.

An error is raised if a chunk contains a number of lines that is not a multiple of four, as this indicates a malformed FASTQ file or an incomplete FASTQ record.

See also

open_any, sample_fastq_indices

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Extract selected records from a FASTQ file
keep_lookup <- logical(100000)
keep_lookup[c(10, 100, 1000)] <- TRUE

extract_fastq_records(
  fastq = "reads.fastq",
  outfile = "subset.fastq",
  keep_lookup = keep_lookup,
  total = 100000
)

# The same function works with gzip-compressed files
extract_fastq_records(
  fastq = "reads.fastq.gz",
  outfile = "subset.fastq.gz",
  keep_lookup = keep_lookup,
  total = 100000
)
} # }
